note: Attacker-controlled bytes of a Global section initializer expression (i32.const 1; if ... else ... end) are handed to the parser-only expression walker Parse_InitExpr.
A parser-only M3Compilation is created on the stack with runtime = NULL: no runtime context exists while parsing module sections.
The parse-only walker dispatches the init-expression opcodes into the normal compiler machinery (Compile_BlockStatements) even though this pass never emits code and has no runtime.
The 'if' opcode (0x04) present in the init expression has a compiler entry (Compile_If) and is dispatched to the full compiler handler instead of being rejected in the parser-only pass.
After compiling the if-then block, o->previousOpcode is 'else' (0x05), so Compile_If decides that an else block must be compiled via CompileElseBlock.
Compiling the else branch requires acquiring a code page, but this parser-only compilation has o->runtime == NULL.
The NULL runtime from the parser-only compilation (o->runtime == NULL) is passed into the code-page acquisition machinery.
The NULL runtime is forwarded unchanged into AcquireCodePageWithCapacity.

The compiler accesses code page state through the invalid list pointer &i_runtime->pagesOpen where i_runtime == NULL; RemoveCodePageOfCapacity dereferences it (*io_list), causing a null-pointer dereference crash.
